subject: MLB posting system
query: what is the posting system in mlb
title: What is the posting system in MLB? 2026 window closes Dec. 16
answer: The posting system is how a player under contract with a Japanese (NPB) or Korean (KBO) team can sign with an MLB club. His team "posts" him, all 30 MLB teams can negotiate, and the signing club pays his old team a release fee. Japanese players get a 45-day window; Korean players get 30 days.
body:
Under MLB's agreements with NPB and the KBO, the release fee is 20% of the first $25 million of a major league contract, 17.5% of the next $25 million and 15% of anything above $50 million, plus a 15% supplemental fee on earned bonuses, escalators and exercised options. A deal must be signed by 5 p.m. ET on the final day of the window. If a player does not sign, he returns to his team for the next season and cannot be posted again until the following offseason.

In November 2026, Hanshin Tigers infielder Teruaki Sato, Seibu Lions pitcher Kaima Taira and Nippon-Ham Fighters pitcher Hiromi Itoh were posted; their window runs until Dec. 16, 2026. Korean infielder Si-Hwan Roh of the Hanwha Eagles has a 30-day window that ends Dec. 1. MLB's labor contract with the players' union also expires Dec. 1, 2026; during the 2021-22 lockout, posted players were frozen and their windows resumed after the deal was reached on March 10, 2022.
in_the_news: Japan's Teruaki Sato, Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh entered the MLB posting system on Nov. 2, 2026, with a signing deadline of Dec. 16.

faq.q: How long is the MLB posting window?
faq.a: 45 days for players from Japan's NPB and 30 days for players from Korea's KBO.
